key_insight: The paper argues that feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting can be made more efficient by coding multi-view features directly, instead of first generating a full Gaussian scene and compressing it afterward. This shifts the pipeline from a complex "generate-then-compress" design to a more streamlined, differentiable feature-coding approach.
problem_solved: It addresses the inefficiency and complexity of existing feed-forward 3DGS pipelines, which separately encode geometry and appearance after reconstructing the full Gaussian representation. These pipelines often rely on non-differentiable steps and require specialized codecs for different attributes.
method: Use a feed-forward multi-view feature coding framework to encode scene information before full Gaussian generation.
Replace separate geometry/appearance compression with a unified, more differentiable representation pipeline.
Reduce reliance on post-hoc, attribute-specific codec design and non-differentiable operations.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this can simplify deployment of 3D reconstruction systems while improving efficiency and differentiability. It may also make feed-forward 3D scene coding easier to train, optimize, and adapt to real-world multi-view reconstruction tasks.

paper_title: Feed-Forward Multi-View Feature Coding for 3D Gaussian Splatting
